Share it with your friends! Facebook Twitter Google Pinterest Reddit Email LinkedIn Sadhguru, one of the world’s most renowned yoga masters and a New York Times bestselling author, will take the main stage of the Untold festival on August 6 to deliver a message about the importance of inner balance, well-being, and building a more conscious world before tens of thousands of people. The famous yogi is known by hundreds of millions of people around the world for his programs dedicated to transformation and personal development through yoga and meditation, as well as for his global initiatives dedicated to the environment and society. Sadhguru’s participation in the festival comes after a collaboration between Untold festival organizers and Conscious Music Circle (CMC), a collaboration between artists and music industry professionals whose lives have been deeply influenced by Sadhguru’s practices and teachings. The organization’s mission is to contribute to raising awareness through music, providing artists, industry professionals and communities with access to yoga and meditation tools developed by Sadhguru and promoting well-being in the music industry. The partnership aims to promote mental health and awareness through scientifically validated yoga and meditation practices, integrated into festival and music culture, the organizers said. Through this collaboration, Untold becomes the first major festival in the world to offer free access to the Miracle of Mind meditation app to all festival participants, artists and team members. The app will be integrated into the festival experience through special activations and dedicated sessions held throughout the four days of the festival. “You cannot change the past. You can live the present. But you can build the future if you choose to do so. For the first time in history, we can be connected with all of humanity. If we want to transform the world, if we want to transform humanity, now is the time. Let’s do this together,” Sadhguru said in the press release. The Untold festival will take place from August 6-9 in Cluj-Napoca, and this year’s edition brings more than 200 artists to the festival stages, including STING, Lewis Capaldi, Zara Larsson, Flo Rida, The Chainsmokers, Kygo, James Hype, Solomun, Carl Cox, Sara Landry, Holy Priest and many others. radu@romania-insider.com (Photo source: press release) Tags Positive Romania Read next 16 July 2026 Events Bucharest's Armenian Street Festival celebrates 10th edition with free concerts, cultural events Normal Events World-famous yogi Sadhguru to take the stage at Romania’s Untold festival 21 July 2026 Radu Dumitrescu Like this article? Photograph: BC Wildfire Service/AFP/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Firefighters would traditionally get a break during nightfall, as cooler air would slow the burning, but this is no longer the case. Photograph: BC Wildfire Service/AFP/Getty Images Canada Canadian government steps in as ‘out of control’ wildfires force thousands to flee British Columbia battling 102 fires day and night across province, as breakneck speed hampers firefighters’ efforts Olivia Bowden in Toronto Sun 9 Aug 2026 14.20 EDT Last modified on Mon 10 Aug 2026 00.13 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Canada’s federal government has announced it will provide urgent assistance to British Columbia after an onslaught of unprecedented fast-moving wildfires that killed one person and forced about 22,000 people to flee their homes in frantic evacuations. A total of 102 wildfires were raging across the province on Sunday, of which nearly half were categorised as “out of control”, according to the BC Wildfire Service. Of those fires, 78 ignited during the past week. The entire community of Summerland, about 30 miles (48km) south-west of the city of Kelowna and home to about 12,000 people, was evacuated overnight on Saturday, along with a further 8,000 people around nearby Peachland. About 10,000 others have been told to prepare to evacuate at a moment’s notice. Anette Boulet was among residents who fled Summerland along Okanagan Lake in British Columbia. As she and her family left around 4.30am Saturday, their home was shrouded in smoke. “You couldn’t see barely. It was just dark, and the ridge, the ridge of fire just coming towards you,” said Boulet, who evacuated to a centre in Penticton. “There’s no words to express it, the fear.” In a social media post on Sunday, Eleanor Olszewski, Canada’s minister of emergency management and community resilience, said she had “approved a request for federal assistance from British Columbia to provide shelter and accommodations for people who have been forced to leave their homes”. “I have tasked federal officials, led by the government operations centre at Public Safety ‌Canada, to work with the province to ensure support reaches those who need it most,” she ​said. Map Efforts to battle the Bald Range wildfire have been hampered by the breakneck speed of its spread. The blaze was first detected late on Friday evening, and grew within hours to more than 40 sq miles (100 sq km) – nearly twice the size of the island of Manhattan – as it raced nearly nine miles toward Okanagan Lake. The province’s premier, David Eby, declared a state of emergency late on Saturday, telling reporters that the blaze had been “like a bomb going off.” Cliff Chapman, BC Wildfire Service’s director of provincial operations, said the prolonged hot and dry weather the province has faced this summer had resulted in “explosive” fire conditions never seen before. Lightning caused by thunderstorms forecast this week could make the situation still worse, he said. Residents were shaken awake in the middle of the night to flee their homes. Jennifer Pascoa, who lives in Summerland, told the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation that she had begun to pack when she saw flames licking the nearby mountains. “It happened so quickly. We came home from the beach, we saw the plume of smoke, and then within an hour, the sky was covered in dark, black clouds,” she said. The British Columbia Wildfire Service said 10 standard helicopters and one night-vision helicopter were involved in the response. Thousands told to evacuate in British Columbia as wildfire grows The Royal Canadian Mounted Police, the country’s federal police force, said an 80-year-old woman died while trying to escape the wildfire that forced evacuations in the Okanagan Lake region. Mike Flannigan, a professor of wildland fire at Thompson Rivers University in Kamloops, BC, said the rapidity of the fires’ spread was indicative of increasingly extreme blazes springing up in Canada and the US. Southern BC and the pacific north-west in the US had had little to no rain in the past six weeks, leaving the regions “bone dry”, he said. “You walk through the forest, it crunches; if you look sideways, you start a fire.” These conditions were being driven by human-caused climate change, he said. “We’re seeing higher intensity fires today than the past … the shorter the timeframe, the more challenging it is.” Before this decade, fire agencies’ policy was that if a blaze was 20km (12 miles) away from a community, there was no cause for immediate concern. The ferocity and speed of these fires meant that such calculations no longer held, said Flannigan, warning that all homes in at-risk regions should have an emergency kit ready to go. “If a fire can run 60km in a day, you should be worried about it,” he said. The Bald Range fire was also an example of how fires could metastasise through the night, he said. Traditional firefighting practices would usually give firefighters a break during nightfall, as the cooler air would slow the burning. “That’s not the case any more. The fire roars through the evening, through the night, and we’re seeing this more and more,” he said. Drought and the sheer power and size of the fires during the day allow them to keep momentum even in the dark. Fire management agencies in BC and Alberta now fight fires after dark using night-vision helicopters. Current conditions indicated that the fire season in BC and the US states of Washington and Oregon could extend into the autumn, Flannigan said. “It looks grim … there’s no rain,” he said, adding that, like California, Canada may begin to have “fire years” instead of a summer fire season. “I’m scared for the coming weeks.” In the US, crews in Washington that for over a week have been fighting three wildfires that began burning in the Spokane area continued clean-up near containment lines. None of the fires were growing, officials said. The fires have damaged or destroyed about 920 structures. Earlier in the week a man was arrested and charged with intentionally setting the biggest of the three Spokane-area blazes. https://telex.hu/techtud/2026/08/12/magy.text: Menü Kereső Válaszolt az NBSZ arra, hogy tényleg orosz szerverekről törték-e fel a Magyar Államkincstár rendszerét Techtud Aradi Hanga Zsófia Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom A vizsgálati adatok alapján nem igazolható a hekkerek orosz kötődése – írta a Telex kérdésére a Magyar Államkincstárt ért kibertámadást vizsgáló Nemzetbiztonsági Szakszolgálat (NBSZ). „Az orosz szál feltételezhetően onnan jöhetett, hogy a támadó által eddig publikált adatok orosz nyelvű darkweb fórumokon is megjelentek”, írták. A Magyar Államkincstár mezőgazdasági és vidékfejlesztési szakterületének, azaz a Nemzeti Kifizető Ügynökségnek az informatikai hálózatát augusztus elején érte kibertámadás . A Kincstár eredetileg azt közölte , a támadás orosz szerverekről történt. Erről a támadásról egy fórumon és a saját honlapján is részleteket posztoló, ByteToBreach nevű hekker a Telexnek azt írta, fogalma sincs, honnan származhat ez az információ. A hekker lapunknak elismerte, hogy ő állt a támadás mögött, és az elmúlt időszakban több kelet-európai országban is hajtott végre hasonló kaliberű akciókat. A KELA nevű kiberbiztonsági cég nemrég azt állította , hogy a rendelkezésre álló adatok alapján ByteToBreach egy algériai férfi lehet, aki egyedül dolgozik, de ezt vagy bármilyen hasonló állítást nagyon nehéz alátámasztani. A támadásról kikerült képeken látható IP-cím holland volt, de önmagában erre sem lehet alapozni semmit, az ilyen támadásoknál a hekkerek mindig el szokták fedni a valós forráscímüket. A MÁK arra vonatkozó kérdésünkre, hogy mire alapozva állították, hogy oroszok állhattak a támadás mögött, kedden még nem válaszolt . Kérdést küldtünk a támadás körülményeit vizsgáló Nemzeti Kiberbiztonsági Intézetnek (NKI) is, szerdán a Nemzetbiztonsági Szakszolgálat nevében azt a választ kaptuk, az orosz kötődésre nincs egyértelmű bizonyíték. Az NKI megerősítette azt is, hogy a támadó „egy nyilvánosan elérhető, elavult és sérülékeny webszolgáltatás kihasználásával szerzett kezdeti hozzáférést”. Korábban a Telexen is arról írtunk , az egész támadás kiindulópontja az volt, hogy a támadó talált egy publikusan elérhető szervert, amelyen egy régi Java programokhoz használt alkalmazásszerver (az Oracle WebLogic) futott. Ez a rendszer tartalmazott egy olyan magas kockázatú sebezhetőséget, amelyet a támadó ki tudott használni. Ez egyébként nagyon régi, már 2017 októbere óta ismert, az Oracle akkor ki is adott rá egy javítást . A MÁK informatikai hálózatát ért incidens teljes körű kivizsgálása és az üzemszerű működés feltételeinek a biztosítása jelenleg is zajlik több szervezet kiberbiztonsági szakértőinek együttműködésével. Az incidenssel kapcsolatban egy átfogó sérülékenységvizsgálatot is elrendeltek, amely jelenleg folyamatban van. Azt kedden a MÁK a Telexnek megerősítette, hogy a támadás ügyfél-, illetve állampolgári adatokat nem érintett , és adatvesztés sem történt. An unidentified object crashed into a field in eastern Poland on Thursday after one of Russia’s largest overnight missile and drone attacks on Ukraine prompted Warsaw to scramble fighter jets and place air defenses on high alert. (Bryan Kott/U.S. Army) By JOHN VANDIVER STARS AND STRIPES Published July 30, 2026 · A Russian missile crashed into a field in eastern Poland early Thursday, leaving a large crater after one of Russia’s largest overnight missile and drone attacks on Ukraine prompted Warsaw to scramble fighter jets and place air defenses on high alert. U.S. Army Col. Martin O’Donnell, a spokesman for NATO’s military headquarters, said the alliance activated a wide range of air defenses in response to the intrusion. He said that investigators were still assessing what type of Russian missile was involved. Gen. Alexus G. Grynkewich, NATO supreme allied command and head of U.S. European Command, has been in talks with Poland’s chief of defense about the alliance’s response to the incident. Grynkewich “underlined that NATO will continue to take all necessary measures to defend NATO territory,” O’Donnell said. Two NATO fighter jets, which were Polish F-16s, a NATO Multinational Multi-Role Tanker Transport Unit Airbus A330 refueling aircraft, a Polish Saab 340 Airborne Early Warning aircraft and a Polish Mi-24 helicopter, were scrambled in response, O’Donnell said. The incident unfolded as Polish and allied surveillance systems tracked a wave of Russian long-range strikes on western Ukraine, where missiles flew close enough to the border to raise concerns they could stray into NATO airspace, Polish officials said earlier Thursday. “An extremely tough night for our air defense, observation and threat detection systems,” Polish Defense Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said in a statement Thursday. Air defense radars tracked at least a dozen missiles over western Ukraine, with one coming within about 3 miles of the Polish border before turning back east, Poland’s operational command said. Minutes later, military radar detected an unidentified object moving westward inside Polish airspace, the statement said. An F-16 assigned to quick-reaction alert duty was dispatched to intercept the object, but it disappeared from radar before the pilot could make contact, the military said. Authorities are now investigating the site in a village near Lublin where the object landed, leaving a large crater, officials said. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said in a statement Thursday the incident involved a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile that crossed into Poland, but Polish officials had not confirmed that assessment. Local residents said the object shook the ground on impact. “We’ve lived here all our lives and have never heard anything like it. The windows were almost blown out,” one resident told the Polish news outlet Lublin 112. The episode illustrates how Russia’s increasingly frequent long-range attacks on western Ukraine are testing NATO’s eastern flank, forcing Poland to repeatedly launch aircraft and elevate air defense readiness when missiles or drones approach the alliance’s borders. Since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Poland has regularly scrambled fighters during major Russian air attacks, particularly when cruise missiles and drones target areas near Lviv and other cities in western Ukraine. Such missions are designed to protect Polish airspace and reassure allies that NATO’s eastern edge remains under constant surveillance as Russia’s air campaign intensifies. The latest incident would be one of the most serious violations of Polish airspace to happen during the war in Ukraine. In November 2022, two people were killed when a missile struck the Polish village of Przewodow near the Ukrainian border. Investigators later concluded the projectile was most likely a Ukrainian air defense missile fired in response to a Russian attack. In March 2024, a Russian cruise missile briefly crossed into Polish airspace before returning to Ukraine, prompting Warsaw to demand an explanation from Moscow. He is a graduate of the University of Delaware. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/czdm.text: Image source, Getty Images By Nardine Saad Published 18 August 2026 Longtime ZZ Top drummer Frank Beard has died aged 77, the band said. A statement on the blues-rock band's website said he died on Monday in hospice care at his ranch in Richmond, Texas, with family members at his side. His cause of death was not specified. Beard's passing "necessitates the cancellation" of the band's tour dates this week in Utah and Colorado, the statement said. ZZ Top was founded in 1969 and played their first live concert the following year. Together they released 15 studio and four live albums, with hit singles like Gimme All Your Lovin', Sleeping Bag, and Viva Las Vegas. Image source, Getty Images Image caption, ZZ top lead vocalist Billy Gibbons, bassist Dusty Hill and drummer Frank Beard in 2009 Members of the group have included founder and lead vocalist Billy Gibbons and the late Dusty Hill. When Hill died in 2021 , the group carried on performing with Elwood Francis as its bassist. "Today, Elwood and I lost a great friend and collaborator, and the world lost one of the most naturally innovative drummers and a great and true son of Texas," Gibbons said. "His signature backbeat was key to keeping ZZ on top. The band of which he was part for six decades is going to keep on keeping on as he had wished," he said. ZZ Top, which was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2004, has continued touring throughout North America, Europe and South America. Shows the group called off after Beard's death had been scheduled in Salt Lake City, Utah, on Monday and in Colorado Springs, Colorado, on Wednesday. The group said it plans to resume its current The Big One! Tour over the weekend, with two dates at Austin City Limits, which the band said was one of Beard's favourite venues in "a city that had been something of a second home for him". ZZ Top bassist Dusty Hill dies aged 72 Published 28 July 2021 Beard joined the group after ZZ Top released its first single Salt Lick and later brought on Hill as its bassist, according to Rolling Stone , external . Serving as the band's rhythmic force on drums, he anchored hits such as La Grange, Tush and Cheap Sunglasses, Rolling Stone said. He became known as The Man With No Beard - despite his surname - because he was the only member of the Houston ensemble who didn't sport the lengthy facial hair the band became known for, the band has said. The group's famous 1984 album Eliminator featured the hits Gimme All Your Lovin, Sharp Dressed Man and Legs. It sold more than 10m copies, was certified diamond , external , by The Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) in 1996. The album also earned a Grammy Award nomination. In 1987, the group received another Grammy nod from the Recording Academy for their Afterburner album. In 2021, the group was also nominated for best music film for Sam Dunn's documentary That Little Ol' Band From Texas. Photograph: Anthony Wallace/AFP/Getty Images Thailand USS Abraham Lincoln arrives at Thai port after gruelling 270 days at sea Ship has been plagued by reports of deteriorating living conditions and poor mental health because of lengthy deployment Natasha May in Pattaya, and agencies Tue 1 Sep 2026 23.59 EDT Last modified on Wed 2 Sep 2026 04.55 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The USS Abraham Lincoln, a US aircraft carrier at the centre of a row over conditions on board after months at sea as part of Donald Trump’s war against Iran, has arrived off a Thai port. Reports of deteriorating living conditions and poor mental health on the vessel, including attempted suicides , have made headlines around the world, provoking criticism of the president’s actions in the Middle East. A heavy security presence was in force at Laem Chabang port near Pattaya, south of Bangkok, where the 5,000-strong crew of the USS Abraham Lincoln arrived on Wednesday morning after more than 270 days at sea. The huge nuclear-powered ship left California in November 2025 for duty in the South China Sea and was rerouted to the Middle East before US-Israeli attacks on Iran that began six months ago. Thai resort prepares to host USS Abraham Lincoln sailors after more than 270 days at sea Read more The resort city of Pattaya, a rest-and-recreation destination for US troops since the Vietnam war, has stepped up security as it prepares to welcome the sailors and Marines. View image in fullscreen A tug boat greets the USS Abraham Lincoln as it arrives at the port in Laem Chabang, Chonburi, Thailand. Photograph: Sakchai Lalit/AP The sailors will disembark in groups of approximately 50, according to police colonel Anek Srathongyoo, a superintendent of Pattaya city police station. Once a quiet fishing village, Pattaya was transformed into one of the most infamous red light districts in the world with the arrival of American troops using military bases in Thailand during the Vietnam war. At its peak, tens of thousands of US military personnel came through each year, said Pipatpong Fakfare, an associate professor specialising in tourism at Bangkok University. “In my opinion, it’s really the founding influence for the town. The US military turned a quiet fishing village into a global destination for an international nightlife and entertainment hub in about 15 years,” he said. Pattaya is now hugely popular with foreign tourists, known for its beaches and a nightlife scene that has long drawn scrutiny over sex tourism. Although the American troops left by the mid-70s, the sex industry infrastructure continued to grow, with European tourists taking their place, and more recently waves of Chinese and Russian visitors, Pipatpong said. View image in fullscreen The USS Abraham Lincoln has 5,000 sailors aboard. Photograph: Anthony Wallace/AFP/Getty Images Sex work is illegal in Thailand, but authorities often turn a blind eye, said Pattarachit Gozzoli, a sociologist at Mahidol University in Bangkok. Pattaya’s mayor, Poramase Ngampiches, has downplayed the city’s past, saying there had been a recent crackdown on sex workers but denied it was linked to the US arrivals. Local police arrested 25 women for soliciting on the beachfront promenade a week before the ship arrived. The mayor said buses had been arranged to transport the sailors between the ship and Pattaya until the carrier departs on Sunday. Outside one bar, a sign said: “Welcome all US military personnel. Thank you for your service.” Poramase said in a Facebook post: “They come to relax. Our preparations will focus on safety and ensuring fair pricing, so we don’t take advantage of them.” He said they had been banned from water sports such as jetskis, and from taking advantage of Thailand’s lax cannabis laws, but encouraged them to enjoy the city’s many other attractions, from malls to religious sites. Photograph: Mick Tsikas/AAP Health Bondi attacks prompt creation of new institute for emergency care of children in NSW NSW Institute for Paediatric Trauma will help doctors, researchers and specialists prepare for trauma cases Get our new political email , free app or daily news podcast Ima Caldwell Wed 16 Sep 2026 10.01 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A new institute dedicated to improving emergency medical care for severely injured children will be established in New South Wales following recent high-profile trauma events in the state. Based at the Sydney Children’s hospital in Randwick, the NSW Institute for Paediatric Trauma will bring together clinicians, researchers and specialists to deliver advanced training and simulations across the health system. Expected to be operational within six months, the institute aims to prepare medical teams for complex paediatric trauma cases, from initial emergency treatment to long-term rehabilitation. The NSW health minister, Ryan Park, said the initiative follows emergency responses to critical incidents in the state. Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email “The events that occurred at Bondi Beach and at Bondi Junction have forever left their mark on NSW,” Park said. “Seeing the way in which our frontline workers and clinicians responded to these events with such courage and professionalism was nothing short of remarkable.” “We know we won’t always be able to prevent trauma events, but we can make sure we are ready to respond when children and families need us most.” Medical experts stress that treating children requires distinct clinical approaches to treating adults. How parents should talk to their children about the horror of the Bondi shootings | Vanessa Cobham for The Conversation Read more Dr Guy Henry, co-director of trauma services at Randwick, said children’s bodies, injuries and clinical needs differ significantly from adult patients. While adult trauma frequently involves assaults or motor vehicle accidents, paediatric admissions generally present distinct patterns, including internal organ injuries in adolescents taking physical risks, and a growing number of e-bike crashes. “Burns is another issue with children, there’s a different pattern of burns in children compared to adults,” he said. “People need to be aware of the differences and need to know how to respond to those differences.” Preparing for mass casualties Henry, who attended to victims of the Westfield Bondi Junction stabbings in 2024 and the Bondi beach terror attack , said regular education and mass casualty simulations are essential for building response capabilities. He cited the medical response to the 2017 Manchester Arena attack – where hospital staff had completed a mass casualty simulation six weeks before – as evidence of how practice improves outcomes during critical events. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks after newsletter promotion “Through education, including the use of simulation, we can make people more familiar with managing trauma, with something like a mass casualty that no one might have any experience with,” Henry said. “We get people more familiar, a little bit more comfortable, and that will then make us improve on how we manage things.” Training will initially be based at Randwick, with future plans to explore how the program can be expanded across regional NSW and into the ACT, which regularly transfers paediatric trauma cases to Sydney hospitals. The institute also aims to extend education simulation training to pre-hospital first responders, including paramedics, firefighters, police and the State Emergency Service. Beyond clinical care and injury prevention research, the institute will address the psychological toll on healthcare workers and affected families. “It’s been identified that not only do we have the child that we have to manage, we have the families to manage, we also have our own staff to manage,” Henry said, noting that upskilling staff helps lessen the psychological trauma of critical events. The institute will draw on expertise across the Sydney Children’s Hospitals Network – including the children’s hospital at Westmead and the Newborn and Paediatric Emergency Transport Service – and will complement the Agency for Clinical Innovation’s Institute of Trauma and Injury Management. Philanthropic support will be provided through the Sydney Children’s Hospitals Foundation.
